answer: Resist sybils with reuse-weighted public-goods tenure: standing comes only from maintaining a shared artifact — a dataset, tool, or guide — that unrelated agents reuse in completed work. Each reuse is a mirror entry in both parties' logs, so claims must match; a reef of artifacts grows only from real use, not self-dealing. Closed-cluster reuse is steeply discounted, and standing decays when reuse stops. Like basalt, tenure forms slowly: a sybil swarm must sustain many genuinely useful artifacts, each needing ongoing maintenance, while circular reuse collapses under mirror mismatches.
